This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, praying to modify the judgment and award dated 29.08.2022 passed by the Sr.Civil Judge, Jewargi M.A.C.T.XV, Jewargi in MVC No.798/2020 and be pleased to allow the claim petition by granting the relief as prayed for by the appellants herein in the interest of justice and equity.

This appeal having been heard and reserved on 16.03.2023 coming on for pronouncement of judgment, this day Ramachandra D.Huddar J., delivered the following :
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the appellants/petitioners challenging the judgment and award passed by the Sr.Civil Judge and JMFC and M.A.C.T-XV, Jewargi (in short `the Tribunal') in MVC No.798/2020 dated 29.08.2022, on the ground of inadequate and meager compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are;
The petitioners are the parents of the deceased Mahiboob S/o Hussain Basha Kukanoor, aged 21 years.
That on 04.04.2020 at about 4.30 p.m. the deceased was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-32/EN-9857 and was proceeding towards Jubilee Petrol bunk to fill petrol to his motorcycle.

At that time, the driver of tractor bearing registration No.KA-32/TB-2984 came from Shahapur side and was proceeding towards Jewargi main road and when said Mahiboob was near Mirchi weigh bridge, the said tractor driver came from opposite direction in a high speed and in the negligent manner and without giving any signal, turned the tractor towards right side and dashed to the motorcycle of Mahiboob.

Due to the collision, the said Mahiboob sustained severe injuries and was shifted to Government Hospital for treatment and thereafter he was shifted to United Hospital for higher treatment at Kalaburagi.

But, later during the treatment said Mahiboob died on 5.4.2020 and a case was registered against the tractor driver under Crime No.62/2020 at Jewargi Police Station.
4.
It is stated that the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 21 years and was working in the puncture garage at Jewargi and thereby he used to earn `25,000/- per month.
The deceased was the only earning member of the family, who used to look after the petitioners and the family was depending on his income.
In view of the sudden and untimely death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their bread earner, love and affection and also have suffered mentally and financially.
The deceased was the earning member of the family and after his death there is no one in the family to take responsibility of the petitioners and to bear the family expenses.
Hence, they filed a claim petition seeking compensation.

sentences.text: On service of notice, respondent-Insurance Company appeared and filed detailed statement of objections denying inter alia age, avocation and income including the death of deceased as alleged in the claim petition.
It is further pleaded that the accident was not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor but, it was due to negligent act of the deceased himself.

Hence, on this basis,
sought for dismissal of claim petition.
Further, it was averred in the objection statement that there is no cogent evidence before the Court to prove that the respondent drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
So also respondent-1 filed statement of objection denying the petition averments.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the mother of the deceased entered the witness box and examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P23.
Respondents have not adduced any evidence.

7. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary, the Tribunal fastened liability on both the respondents jointly and severally and awarded total compensation of `16,24,400/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed the respondent-Insurance Company to deposit the compensation.

8. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for the appellants/petitioners that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is erroneous, contrary to the material evidence placed on record and the documents presented by the petitioners.

9. Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal has gone wrong in making assessment of income of the deceased to the extent of `10,000/- per month whereas, the income ought to have been taken at `25,000/-.
Even if that is not taken, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the income according to the notional income chart value at `13,750/- for the accident of the year 2020.

Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal has awarded meager compensation under other heads and has not awarded just and reasonable compensation which also requires interference at the hands of this Court.
10. Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal has not awarded suitable compensation under the head 'loss of consortium' to the dependants/legal representatives of the deceased.
He further contends that the Tribunal has committed a gross error in not adding 'loss of future prospects' to the income of the deceased.
On these grounds, they seek enhancement of compensation and consequently to allow the appeal.

11. Per contra, learned counsel Sri Subhash Mallapur, appearing on behalf of respondent-Insurance Company vehemently contends that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is in consonance with the material evidence placed on record and the same in fact, is on the higher side.

Learned counsel further contends that the award of compensation on the other heads are suitably calculated and rightly awarded, which do not call for interference and on the basis of these submissions, he seeks to dismiss the appeal filed by the petitioners.

sentences.text:
Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants/petitioners and learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are:
i) Whether the petitioners are entitled to enhancement of compensation?
ii) What order"
13.

On a careful perusal of entire material on record and having gone through the impugned judgment and award including the exhibits marked in the case on hand, it is apparently seen that the petitioners would be entitled for enhancement of compensation for the reason stated herein below:-
(a) It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 04.04.2020 at 4.30 p.m. between tractor and motorbike leading to the death of deceased-Mahiboob S/o Hussain Basha.
These aspects have been proved by way of production of Ex.P1 to P10 which are police records.
Admittedly, there is no challenge made to the initiation of criminal prosecution and laying of charge-sheet.
The Insurance Company has not filed any appeal against the judgment and award.

Under the circumstances, there is no requirement for this Court to delve into the occurrence of accident, involvement of the vehicles and so also the death having occurred due to the road traffic accident.
(b) Now, the question that is to be decided by this Court is whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager and whether calls for interference by this Court.

(c) In this regard, it is relevant to quote the decision in Syed Basheer Ahmed vs. Mohammed Zameer1 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court noticed that Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act enjoins the claims Tribunal to make an award determining "the amount of compensation which appears to be just".

entities.text: Syed Basheer Ahmed vs. Mohammed Zameer1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the objective factors, which may constitute the basis of compensation appearing as just, have not been indicated in the Act.
Thus, the expression "which appears to be just" vests wide discretion in the Claims (2009) 2 SCC 225 Tribunal in the matter of determination of compensation.

Nevertheless, the wide amplitude of such power does not empower the Tribunal to determine the compensation arbitrarily or to ignore settled principles relating to the determination of the compensation.

Similarly, although the Act is a beneficial legislation, it can neither be allowed to be used as a source of profit nor as a windfall to the persons affected nor should it be punitive to the persons liable to pay compensation.

The determination of the compensation must be based on certain data, establishing reasonable nexus between the loss incurred by the dependents of the deceased and the compensation to be awarded to them.
In a nutshell, the amount of compensation determined to be payable to the petitioners has to be fair and reasonable by accepted legal standards.

(d) The determination of the quantum must answer what "contemporary society would deem to be a fair sum such as would allow the wrong doer to hold up his head among his neighbours and say with their approval that he has done the fair thing".
The amount awarded must not be niggardly since the "law values life and limb in a free Society in generous case".

At the same time, misplaced sympathy,

sentences.text: The object of providing compensation is to please the petitioners to the extent possible, in almost the same financial position as they were in before the accident and not to make a fortune out of misfortune that has befallen them.
(e) On the basis of the material evidence placed before this Court, it is seen that the deceased was aged about 21 years and was doing labour work in a garage and was earning `25,000/- per month.
We are in agreement with the learned counsel for the appellants that, `13,750/- requires to be taken as monthly income and same is taken as per notional chart issued by the KSLSA.
The deceased being aged 21 years is entitled to 40% towards future prospects in addition to the notional income chart value for assessment of income.
In view of the fact that the deceased was aged 21 years, the appropriate multiplier would be '18' which is rightly taken by the Tribunal.
Same does not call for interference.

(f) Addition of 40% towards loss of future prospects to be added as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2, which would be `19,250/- (`13,750/- + 5,500 (40%)).

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, as the deceased was a bachelor, 50% would have to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses as contemplated in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another3, which would be `9,625/-
(`19,250/- - 50%) and the appropriate multiplier is '18'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, loss of dependency would be `20,79,000/- (`9,625 X 12 X 18).

(g) We are in agreement with the contentions of the learned counsel for petitioners that the Tribunal has committed error in not awarding appropriate amount towards (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 consortium.

Since the dependents are parents of the deceased, parental consortium is required to be granted at the rate of `40,000/- each as contemplated in the case of Pranay Sethi stated supra,
which has been subsequently followed in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., v. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others4.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., v. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, an amount of `80,000/- (40,000/- X 2) is awarded under the head 'loss of consortium'.

(h) Towards 'loss of estate' and towards 'transportation of dead body & funeral expenses', petitioners would be entitled to `15,000/- each i.e., a sum of `30,000/- requires to be awarded and it is accordingly awarded.
Accordingly, under conventional head `1,10,000/- (loss of consortium `80,000/- + loss of estate `15,000/- + Towards transportation of dead body & funeral expenses `15,000/-) is awarded.

(2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121 AIR 2020 SC 3076 (i) As per the decision in Pranay Sethi, stated supra, 10% on the conventional head for each block period requires to be awarded, which in the present case would be `11,000/- for one block period.
(j) Towards medical expenses a sum of `32,400/- has been awarded by the Tribunal, same is retained.

The tractor involved in the accident is insured with the respondent No.2,

The Judgment and Award dated 29.08.2022 passed in MVC No.798/2020 by the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, MACT, Jewargi is modified.
The appellants-petitioners are held entitled for enhanced compensation of `6,08,000/- together with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

The respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the said enhanced compensation before the Senior Civil Judge & MACT-XV, Jewargi within four weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
